title: Potted Shrimp
subtitle: British brown shrimps in spiced butter
excerpt: Potted shrimp is one of the great traditional foods of Britain: tiny brown shrimps cooked briefly in spiced butter with mace, cayenne, and nutmeg, then packed into small pots and covered with clarified butter to seal and preserve them. The shrimps are eaten at room temperature spread on thin toast. The flavour combination of sweet shrimp, spice, and butter is remarkable.
sourceNotes: Potted shrimps have been made on the Lancashire coast since at least the 18th century. The town of Morecambe Bay is particularly associated with potted shrimps -- the bay's brown shrimps (Crangon crangon) are considered the best in Britain. The potting technique uses butter and spice to preserve the shrimps for several days. The dish appears in Hannah Glasse's 1747 cookbook The Art of Cookery Made Plain and Easy.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make up to 3 days ahead. Keep refrigerated under the butter seal.

content.text: Brown shrimps are much smaller than regular prawns -- tiny, sweet, and delicate. They are sold cooked and peeled from good fishmongers and online. If you cannot find brown shrimps, small cooked North Atlantic prawns can be substituted, but the result is less sweet and more assertive. Serve with thin brown bread toast and lemon wedges.

Melt 100 g of {{unsalted-butter}} butter in a pan over low heat. Add {{mace-ground}} mace, {{cayenne-pepper}} cayenne, {{nutmeg}} nutmeg, and {{salt-table}} salt. Stir for 30 seconds. Add {{brown-shrimps}} shrimps and stir gently to coat. Warm through for 2 minutes -- do not boil. Add {{lemon}} lemon juice. Divide between 4 small ramekins.

Melt the remaining 50 g of {{unsalted-butter}} butter in a clean pan over very low heat. Pour through a sieve to clarify. Spoon a thin layer of the clarified butter over the shrimps in each ramekin to seal. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour until set. Remove from the fridge 20 minutes before serving. Serve with thin brown toast.

items.symptom: The shrimps taste bland and lack depth
items.cause: The spices were not warmed in the butter first.
items.fix: The spices must be added to the melted butter and stirred for 30 seconds before the shrimps go in. This blooms the spices and infuses their flavour into the fat, which then coats every shrimp.

content.text: Potted shrimps are one of the great traditional British foods. They are closely associated with Morecambe Bay in Lancashire, where the local brown shrimps have been potted and sold since the 18th century. The dish is now sold throughout Britain in glass jars and served as a classic starter in British restaurants. It is one of the food traditions that has survived continuous production for over 300 years.
